def-finite-straight-line-computational-p:
## Definition

Fix an input dimension $n\ge0$, finitely many operation nodes $1,\ldots,T$, and an output node $o$ whose value space is $\mathbb R$. Input coordinate $i$ has value $x_i$. Operation node $j$ has an ordered list of parent slots $p_{j,1},\ldots,p_{j,r_j}$; each slot points to an input or an operation with index less than $j$. Repeated parent slots are allowed and count separately. The graph is a finite straight-line program because every operation reads only earlier values and there are no data-dependent loops.

For each operation $j$, choose a finite-dimensional real value space $E_j$, an open set $U_j\subseteq E_{p_{j,1}}\times\cdots\times E_{p_{j,r_j}}$, and a primitive map $\phi_j:U_j\to E_j$. A smooth primitive is $C^1$: it is totally differentiable and its derivative matrix is continuous. For Hessian-vector products require the primitive to be $C^2$, meaning $C^1$ with a continuously differentiable derivative map. The real-arithmetic primal recursion is $z_j=\phi_j(z_{p_{j,1}},\ldots,z_{p_{j,r_j}})$ whenever the parent tuple lies in $U_j$. Its admissible input domain is the set of $x\in\mathbb R^n$ for which every operation in this recursion is defined.

The **primal tape** is the finite ordered record of input and node values, parent-slot indices, primitive identities, and (when applicable) selected branch labels. A deterministic replay starts from the identical checkpoint state and applies the identical primitive maps in the identical order, so it reproduces the same real-arithmetic values and local derivative inputs. Opaque solver calls are not primitive operations unless their complete deterministic map and derivative rule are explicitly supplied.

A piecewise-$C^1$ primitive is specified by finitely many open branch regions and a $C^1$ formula on each region; its primal boundary value, if any, is specified separately. If the current parent tuple lies strictly inside exactly one declared branch, the program uses that branch and its derivative. At a branch boundary or ambiguous branch selection, forward or reverse AD returns NONDIFFERENTIABLE; it does not silently choose a subgradient or generalized derivative. If no primal value is specified at a boundary, that input is outside the program's domain. All correctness theorems below apply on a fixed strict branch. The same convention applies to piecewise-$C^2$ primitives for Hessian-vector products.
lem-implicit-sensitivity-error-controlle:
## Statement

Let $R(z,\theta)$ be $C^2$ near an exact solution $R(z_*,\theta_0)=0$, with $A(z)=R_z(z,\theta_0)$ invertible and $B(z)=R_\theta(z,\theta_0)$. The implicit sensitivity at a state $z$ is $S(z)=-A(z)^{-1}B(z)$. Suppose the local inverse $\Psi$ of $z\mapsto R(z,\theta_0)$, supplied near $z_*$ by the implicit function theorem, is defined on a convex residual neighborhood containing $0$ and $r=R(\tilde z,\theta_0)$, with $\|D\Psi(y)\|\le\kappa$ along their segment. Suppose also that the segment from $z_*$ to $\tilde z=\Psi(r)$ lies in a convex neighborhood where $\|A(z)^{-1}\|\le M$, $\|B(z)\|\le B_0$, and $A,B$ are Lipschitz with constants $L_A,L_B$. Then
$$\|S(\tilde z)-S(z_*)\|\le\kappa\bigl(M^2L_AB_0+ML_B\bigr)\|r\|.$$
This bounds the implicit sensitivity formula evaluated at an approximate state. It is not by itself a bound for the derivative of a stopped iteration.
thm-implicit-differentiation-forward-and:
## Statement

Let $R:\Theta\times Z\to\mathbb R^m$ be $C^1$, where $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p$ and $Z\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ are open. Suppose $R(\theta_0,z_0)=0$ and the state Jacobian $R_z(\theta_0,z_0)$ is invertible. The Euclidean implicit function theorem gives a local $C^1$ solution branch $z=\phi(\theta)$, and
$$D\phi(\theta_0)=-R_z(\theta_0,z_0)^{-1}R_\theta(\theta_0,z_0).$$
For a scalar $C^1$ objective $J(\theta,z)$, its derivative along that branch is
$$D(J(\theta,\phi(\theta)))|_{\theta_0}=J_\theta-J_zR_z^{-1}R_\theta.$$
Equivalently, if $\lambda$ solves $R_z^T\lambda=J_z^T$, this derivative is $J_\theta-\lambda^TR_\theta$. These formulas concern the exact local solution branch; differentiating a stopped iteration is a separate finite-map derivative.
alg-forward-mode-automatic-differentiati:
## Definition

Input a graph from [[def-finite-straight-line-computational-program]], an admissible point $x$, and a direction $v\in\mathbb R^n$. Evaluate all primal node values in topological order and store the tape. Set each input tangent to $\dot x_i=v_i$. For each operation $j=1,\ldots,T$, compute
$$\dot z_j=D\phi_j(z_{p_{j,1}},\ldots,z_{p_{j,r_j}})(\dot z_{p_{j,1}},\ldots,\dot z_{p_{j,r_j}}).$$
Return the primal scalar output $z_o$ and tangent $\dot z_o$. If the input is outside the admissible domain, return DOMAIN_ERROR; if a piecewise primitive is at a branch boundary or has no unique strict active branch, return NONDIFFERENTIABLE and no tangent. All derivative evaluations in this definition are exact real-arithmetic operations on the specified primitive maps.
alg-reverse-mode-automatic-differentiati:
## Definition

Input a graph from [[def-finite-straight-line-computational-program]] and an admissible point $x$. Evaluate and store all primal values in topological order. Initialize every operation cotangent to zero and set the scalar output cotangent $\bar z_o=1$. For $j=T,T-1,\ldots,1$, and for every parent slot $k=1,\ldots,r_j$, accumulate
$$\bar z_{p_{j,k}}\mathrel{+}=D_k\phi_j(z_{p_{j,1}},\ldots,z_{p_{j,r_j}})^T\bar z_j.$$
If the same parent node occurs in multiple slots, add every slot contribution. Return $z_o$ and the cotangents of the input coordinates as the gradient. A point outside the admissible domain returns DOMAIN_ERROR; a branch boundary or ambiguous active branch returns NONDIFFERENTIABLE and no gradient. The procedure differentiates the real-arithmetic graph; it makes no floating-point error claim.
lem-finite-straight-line-program-defines:
## Statement

For a finite straight-line program whose primitives are $C^1$, the recursively defined admissible input domain is open on each fixed strict branch. The scalar output $f$ is $C^1$ there, and its total derivative is obtained by the ordinary chain rule through the primitive maps.

## Statement

If every primitive of a finite straight-line program is $C^2$ on the selected open branch domains, then the real-arithmetic scalar output is $C^2$ on each fixed strict branch.
alg-checkpointed-reverse-schedules:
## Definition

The input is a finite sequence of deterministic $C^1$ transitions $F_1,\ldots,F_T$ between open subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, with starting state $x_0$. Every transition is evaluated on one fixed strict branch and has its exact local reverse rule. The last transition has scalar output and may be the terminal objective, so its scalar cotangent is $1$. A transition tape stores the local values needed by its exact reverse rule. A deterministic replay applies the same transition maps, in the same order, to the identical checkpoint state and therefore reproduces the same values and local derivative inputs. The procedure returns the terminal output and cotangent at $x_0$; an invalid domain evaluation returns DOMAIN_ERROR, and a branch boundary returns NONDIFFERENTIABLE. A checkpoint schedule is permitted only when its saved states and all deterministic replays lie in these declared domains.

**Uniform-block mode.** For $T=0$, return $x_0$ and the supplied cotangent without work. For $T\ge1$, require an integer slot budget $m\ge1$, set $q=\lceil T/m\rceil$, and during one forward pass save $x_{jq}$ for $j=0,\ldots,\lceil T/q\rceil-1$ (all indices are below $T$). This uses at most $m$ saved states. Partition the steps into blocks $[a,b]$ with $a=jq$ and $b=\min(a+q,T)$. Process the blocks from last to first. Within one block, for $\ell=b,b-1,\ldots,a+1$, restore $x_a$, replay $F_{a+1},\ldots,F_{\ell-1}$ without recording, evaluate $F_\ell$ once while recording its local tape, apply its reverse rule to the current cotangent, and discard the one-step tape and replay workspace. Retain only the checkpoint states, the live state/cotangent, and the ordinary one-step reverse tape. Do not infer any optimality property of this schedule.

**Binomial mode.** Define $C(d,0)=C(0,t)=1$, and $C(d,t)=C(d-1,t)+C(d,t-1)$ for integers $d,t\ge1$. The recursive procedure REVERSE$(a,N,d,t,x_a,\bar x_{a+N})$ requires $0\le N\le C(d,t)$ and a known starting state $x_a$. If $N=0$, return the unchanged cotangent. If $N=1$, evaluate and record the unique transition, apply its local reverse rule, and return its output and input cotangents. If $N\ge2$, then $d,t\ge1$. Put $L=\min(N-1,C(d,t-1))$, $R=N-L$; replay the first $L$ transitions from $x_a$ without recording and save the resulting midpoint state $x_{a+L}$. Call REVERSE$(a+L,R,d-1,t,x_{a+L},\bar x_{a+N})$ on the right block. Release the midpoint checkpoint, restore the caller's supplied $x_a$, and call REVERSE$(a,L,d,t-1,x_a,\bar x_{a+L})$ on the left block, where $\bar x_{a+L}$ is the cotangent returned by the right call. Return the right call's terminal value and the left call's cotangent at $x_a$. The top-level call uses $a=0,N=T$, with the specified terminal cotangent. A recursive call with $N>1$ and $d=0$ or $t=0$ is a schedule failure; the capacity condition makes that branch unreachable.

The parameter $d$ bounds the number of simultaneously saved state snapshots. The parameter $t$ bounds, for each transition, the number of additional unrecorded forward evaluations beyond its one recorded evaluation. Both are finite integer inputs. This mode gives a binomial capacity bound; it does not promise a numerical error estimate or an optimal schedule for arbitrary nonuniform primitive costs. For the storage count in the paired theorem, $R_s$ bounds scalar storage for one full primal state. The binomial recursion may reuse one mutable cotangent workspace: each call consumes its terminal cotangent and returns the cotangent at its start, reusing the same buffer through both children. Let $G$ bound the largest one-step tape and local reverse scratch, the constant number of live cotangent/work vectors, and the scalar call-frame records; it excludes the $d$ saved primal states and one live primal state.
alg-differentiate-finite-fixed-point-ite:
## Definition

Input a $C^1$ map $G(z,\theta)$, a $C^1$ initial-state map $z_0(\theta)$, a parameter $\theta$, and a finite budget $K\ge0$. Form the finite computational graph for $z_{k+1}(\theta)=G(z_k(\theta),\theta)$, $k=0,\ldots,K-1$. Evaluate that graph and run forward mode to compute both $z_K(\theta)$ and its derivative $D_\theta z_K(\theta)$. Return that pair with status ITERATES_DIFFERENTIATED. A primitive-domain failure returns DOMAIN_ERROR; a nonsmooth active-branch switch returns NONDIFFERENTIABLE. This procedure differentiates the $K$-step map actually specified by $G,z_0,K$; it does not substitute the derivative of an exact fixed point.
alg-forward-over-reverse-hessian-vector-:
## Definition

Input a $C^2$ graph, admissible $x$, and direction $v$. First run the forward tangent recurrence to compute every $\dot z_j=Dz_j(x)v$. Set $\bar z_o=1$, $\dot{\bar z}_o=0$, and all other reverse accumulators to zero. In reverse topological order, for each node $j$ and parent slot $k$, let $A_{j,k}=D_k\phi_j(z_{p_{j,1}},\ldots,z_{p_{j,r_j}})$ and update
$$\bar z_{p_{j,k}}\mathrel{+}=A_{j,k}^{T}\bar z_j,\qquad \dot{\bar z}_{p_{j,k}}\mathrel{+}=A_{j,k}^{T}\dot{\bar z}_j+\bigl(DA_{j,k}(z_{p_{j,1}},\ldots,z_{p_{j,r_j}})[\dot z_{p_{j,1}},\ldots,\dot z_{p_{j,r_j}}]\bigr)^{T}\bar z_j.$$
Return the input tangent of the gradient, $(\dot{\bar x}_1,\ldots,\dot{\bar x}_n)$. Repeated parent slots receive separate additions. Outside the admissible domain return DOMAIN_ERROR; at a branch boundary return NONDIFFERENTIABLE. The transpose is the real Euclidean transpose, not a complex adjoint.
thm-forward-mode-computes-directional-de:
## Statement

Let $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be the output of a finite $C^1$ program on a fixed strict branch. For every admissible $x\in\Omega$ and direction $v\in\mathbb R^n$, the forward-mode algorithm returns $Df(x)v$.
thm-reverse-mode-computes-gradient:
## Statement

For a finite $C^1$ program with one scalar output $f$, on a fixed strict branch and at every admissible $x$, the reverse-mode algorithm returns $Df(x)^T1$, the gradient of $f$. More precisely, at any operation node $i$, if its value is temporarily treated as an independent variable and all later operations are recomputed from it, then the accumulated cotangent at $i$ is the derivative of the scalar output with respect to that independent node value.
thm-reverse-mode-work-and-tape-storage-b:
## Statement

Fix a finite set of scalar/vector primitive types with at most $r$ parent slots per operation. Suppose each operation $j$ has primal work $w_j\ge1$, its local vector-Jacobian product costs at most $c w_j$, and accumulating each parent-slot contribution costs at most $a$ operations. Count all state-vector dimensions and input-gradient entries in the primal-tape size $S$. Then the exact reverse-mode algorithm for a scalar output uses at most $(1+c+ar)\sum_{j=1}^T w_j$ operations for the primal evaluation, reverse sweep, and parent accumulations, and stores $O(S)$ scalar entries. Opaque solver calls are excluded unless their primal and derivative costs satisfy the same hypotheses.
thm-checkpointed-reverse-schedules-prese:
## Statement

For the finite-dimensional $C^1$ transition sequences on a fixed strict branch defined in [[alg-checkpointed-reverse-schedules]], provided every schedule replay remains in the declared domains, both schedules return the same terminal value and initial-state cotangent as an uncheckpointed reverse sweep. In uniform-block mode, if $T,m\ge1$, $q=\lceil T/m\rceil$, and the block lengths are $r_1,\ldots,r_s$, the number of additional unrecorded forward evaluations is exactly $\sum_{\ell=1}^s r_\ell(r_\ell-1)/2$, at most $m q(q-1)/2$. At most $m$ checkpoint states are saved, with one live replay state and one local step tape. In binomial mode, $C(d,t)=\binom{d+t}{d}$; any $T\le C(d,t)$ steps can be reversed with at most $d$ saved snapshots, one recorded forward evaluation and one reverse evaluation per step, at most $t$ additional unrecorded forward evaluations per step, total work at most $\widehat W+\overline W+tW$, and storage $G+(d+1)R_s$. Here $W$ is the total cost of one unrecorded full forward pass, $\widehat W$ the sum of recorded one-step forward costs, $\overline W$ the sum of local reverse costs, $R_s$ bounds scalar storage for one primal state, and $G$ bounds the largest one-step tape and local reverse scratch, the constant number of live cotangent/work vectors, and scalar recursion-frame records, excluding saved states and one live primal state.
thm-finite-iteration-sensitivity-bound-a:
## Statement

Let $G(z,\theta)$ be $C^2$ near $(z_*,\theta_0)$, with $z_*=G(z_*,\theta_0)$. Let $D$ be an open convex state neighborhood of $z_*$ on which $G$ is defined and $C^2$ near $D\times\{\theta_0\}$. Assume $G(D,\theta_0)\subseteq D$, $\|G_z(z,\theta_0)\|\le q<1$, and $G_z,G_\theta$ are Lipschitz in $z$ with constants $L_z,L_\theta$. Let the initial map $z_0(\theta)$ be $C^1$ and its iterates remain in $D$. Write $s_*=D\phi(\theta_0)$ for the local exact fixed-point branch supplied by the implicit function theorem, $e_k=D_\theta z_k(\theta_0)$, $\delta_0=\|z_0(\theta_0)-z_*\|$, $d_0=\|e_0-s_*\|$, and $C=L_z\|s_*\|+L_\theta$. For every integer $K\ge1$,
$$\|z_K(\theta_0)-z_*\|\le q^K\delta_0,\qquad \|e_K-s_*\|\le q^K d_0+C K q^{K-1}\delta_0,$$
with $q^0=1$ when $q=0,K=1$. If $R(z,\theta)=z-G(z,\theta)$ and $r_K=R(z_K(\theta_0),\theta_0)$, then $(1-q)\|z_K-z_*\|\le\|r_K\|$. The derivative error is not bounded by the residual alone: for $G(z,\theta)=qz+(1-q)\theta$, $\theta_0=0$, and $z_0(\theta)=0$, every finite $K$ has residual zero at $\theta_0$ but $e_K=1-q^K\ne1=s_*$ when $0<q<1$.
thm-forward-over-reverse-computes-hessia:
## Statement

Let $f$ be the scalar output of a finite $C^2$ graph on a fixed strict branch. At every admissible $x$ and direction $v$, the forward-over-reverse algorithm returns $D(\operatorname{grad} f)(x)v$, the Hessian-vector product $H_f(x)v$. No Hessian symmetry assumption is needed for this identity.
thm-graph-gradient-error-from-local-jaco:
## Statement

For a finite scalar-output graph on one fixed strict branch, associate to each parent-slot edge $e$ the exact local derivative map $A_e$ at the exact real-arithmetic primal values. Suppose a reverse recurrence instead uses local maps $\widetilde A_e$ from the same branch satisfying $\|\widetilde A_e-A_e\|\le\eta_e$, with exact accumulation arithmetic. For an input block $i$, let $\mathcal P(i,o)$ be the finite directed paths from that block to output $o$, and order the edges of a path $\pi=(e_1,\ldots,e_s)$ from input to output. The exact gradient contribution is the transpose of $A_{e_s}\cdots A_{e_1}$, and the perturbed recurrence returns the corresponding sum using $\widetilde A_e$. It obeys
$$\|\widetilde g_i-g_i\|\le\sum_{\pi\in\mathcal P(i,o)}\sum_{\ell=1}^s\eta_{e_\ell}\left(\prod_{r<\ell}\|A_{e_r}\|\right)\left(\prod_{r>\ell}(\|A_{e_r}\|+\eta_{e_r})\right).$$
The bound covers local Jacobian and derivative-evaluation errors represented by $\eta_e$. It does not include roundoff in the reverse accumulation additions.
lem-certified-linear-solve-jacobian-and-:
## Statement

For the real mathematical solve primitive $\phi(A,b)=A^{-1}b$, let $A,B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $b,\widehat x\in\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge1$, and suppose certified exact-residual bounds satisfy
$$\|I-AB\|_2\le d<1,\qquad \|b-A\widehat x\|_2\le\rho,\qquad \|B\|_2\le M,\qquad K=\frac{M}{1-d}.$$
Then $A$ is invertible; writing $x=A^{-1}b$, the fixed linear derivative approximations $\widetilde J_bh=Bh$ and $\widetilde J_AH=-BH\widehat x$ obey
$$\|\widetilde J_b-J_b\|\le\eta_b=Kd,\qquad \|\widetilde J_A-J_A\|\le\eta_A=Kd\|\widehat x\|_2+K^2\rho.$$
Use Euclidean vector norms and Frobenius matrix-input norm. Their adjoints are $B^Tc$ and $-(B^Tc)\widehat x^T$. If these adjoints are evaluated by successful length-$n$ rounded real dots and componentwise outer products, put $t=\gamma_n\|B\|_F$, assuming $nu<1$. The resulting cotangent errors are bounded by $(\eta_b+t)\|c\|_2$ and $[\eta_A+(t+u(M+t))\|\widehat x\|_2]\|c\|_2$, respectively. These are derivative approximations to the mathematical solve map, not derivatives of the rounded program.

The fixed $B$ may be assembled from stored basis-vector solves using a triangular, Cholesky or QR backend; its defect must be certified rather than inferred from a factor residual. Replay must preserve the same $\widehat x,B$ and strict graph branch. Reverse accumulation additions are excluded.
